After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding the reach of its brand-new iPad interface, including a brand-new Mac-style sidebar. Here's what you need to know.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app interface

Although WhatsApp originally began adapting its iOS app to the major Liquid Glass visual overhaul back in October last year, the company didn't bring the new design to the iPad for limited testing until June this year.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the new design includes Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons, and contextual menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on iPhone.

The site's latest report points out that WhatsApp is now rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the original bottom tab bar with a Mac-style sidebar as the default layout.

This sidebar follows the layout already used in WhatsApp for Mac, allowing users to quickly access Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls, Meta AI, and other parts of the app. Users can also hide the sidebar to free up more space for the chat list and conversation view.

Here's the report:

WABetaInfo points out that the new sidebar is already available to some testers using the latest TestFlight version, but some users using the regular App Store version have also started seeing this feature.

As is typical of WhatsApp's rollout approach, the new interface may take some time to reach all users, whether they're on the Beta version or the official version. However, iPad users will eventually benefit from a layout that's better suited to tablets.
